title: Groups
description:
Groups are rather simple: They are used to quickly and easily add permisions to certain people. Imagine each people needing a copy of a file with specific permissions instead of just making a group for each collection of people. You create a group with the command `groupadd <NAME>` (very creative command name, right?), and you delete it with `groupdel <NAME>` (yeah no its bad). To add a user to a group you use `usermod -aG <USER> <GROUP>` and to change the group of a file/dir, you use `chgrp <GROUP> <FILES>`.

---
## Assignment:
What command sequence would you use to create a group developers, add the `main` user to it, then change the group of the `thisfile` file to developers.
b1t: groupadd developers -> usermod -G developers main -> chgrp developers thisfile
b2t: groupadd developers -> usermod -aG developers main -> chgrp developers thisfile
b3t: groupadd developers -> usermod -aG main developers -> chgrp thisfile developers
b4t: usermod -aG developers main -> groupadd developers -> chgrp developers thisfile
